# Asseco BooX — "Your Bank, Out of the Box"

**Marketing campaign brief & communication policy**

Asseco Poland S.A. · Campaign code ACP-BOOX-2026 · Version 1.0
Runs 15 September 2026 – 31 January 2027 · Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Romania, Serbia

---

## The idea in one paragraph

Banks take about two years to launch a new product, because every launch turns into a software
programme. Asseco BooX is a banking platform where the products are already built — you switch them
on and configure them instead of building them. So the whole campaign says one simple thing:
**your bank's next product should take months, not years, and you should not have to replace your
core system to get it.** Everything below is the detailed plan for saying that.

---

## 1. About Asseco

The Asseco Group is present everywhere where technology and business impact everyday life. We are a
federation of companies which operate worldwide, led by Asseco Poland — one of the first startups
established in Poland, today the largest IT company in Central and Eastern Europe and a member of the
WIG30 index.

Our systems are used by banks, energy and telecommunication companies, the public sector and the health
care service. Software from the Asseco Group runs in more than half of the banks operating in Poland.
We know that we cannot fail and we take full responsibility for the projects that we implement. In this
way, we have been building the trust in Asseco and its value for many years.

We have been constantly improving our competencies and investing in research and development, because
the most important thing for us is the success of our customers. That approach has made us the market
leader in Poland, Israel, South-Eastern Europe and Central Europe.

**Tagline:** *Technology for business, solutions for people.*

## 2. The product we are promoting

**Asseco BooX** ("Bank out of the Box") is a ready-made platform for selling and servicing banking
products. Onboarding, loans, deposits, cards, servicing and collections are already built into it, so a
bank configures a new product instead of writing one from scratch.

- It can be the foundation of a completely new bank, or a modern layer on top of the core system a bank
  already has.
- It runs on-premise, in the cloud, or hybrid — the bank chooses.
- It is sold by subscription, or by classic licence.

Where it sits next to the rest of our banking portfolio:

| Product | What it does |
|---|---|
| def3000/suite | Core banking for large commercial banks |
| def2500/suite | Core banking for cooperative and smaller banks |
| **Asseco BooX** | **The product platform on top — new build or modernisation** |
| Customer Banking Platform | The customer-facing sales and service channels |

### The three things we are allowed to claim

1. **Launch a working product in months, not years** — the processes ship with the platform.
2. **Modernise without replacing your core** — BooX wraps what you already run, so you move product by
   product instead of betting the bank on one cutover.
3. **Subscription pricing, Asseco accountability** — pay as you grow, from the vendor that already runs
   more than half of Polish banking.

### What we must never claim

- No client names without that client's written approval. Existing def3000 references are **not**
  cleared for BooX creative.
- No invented numbers ("40% cheaper", "6-week go-live"). The approved phrasing is "months, not years".
- No competitor named. Ever. Not Temenos, not Mambu, not Thought Machine, not anyone.
- No "AI-powered" in the headline. AI is mentioned only in feature copy, only where it actually exists.
- Never imply BooX is free or open source.

## 3. What the campaign is for

Change how banks see Asseco: from "the old core-banking vendor our IT department already knows" to
"the platform partner we would choose for a new digital product".

| Goal | How we measure it | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Awareness of BooX as its own product | Aided recall among CEE banking decision-makers | 18% → 35% |
| Sales pipeline | Qualified opportunities from Tier-2/Tier-3 banks | 60 |
| Perception | Positive or neutral sentiment in professional discussion | at least 70% |
| Technical credibility | Registrations on the API documentation portal | 1,200 |

## 4. Who we are talking to

**Bank executives — the people who sign.** CEO, COO, CFO, Chief Digital Officer at mid-sized banks.
Age 42–60. Squeezed between regulators on one side and fintechs taking their under-35 customers on the
other. Cautious by job description, and personally accountable if a big IT programme fails. They are
buying certainty, not features.

**IT leaders and architects — the people who can kill the deal.** Head of IT, Chief Architect, Head of
Digital Channels. Age 33–50. Most have survived at least one painful vendor migration. They are
sceptical of "out of the box" because they assume it means rigid and impossible to customise. They will
go looking for the API documentation before they answer a sales email. This group decides whether the
campaign looks credible or looks like marketing.

**Trade press and industry watchers.** Not buyers, but they set the tone: Puls Biznesu, Cashless.pl,
Bankier.pl, Finextra, The Banker. Also the regulator's sensitivity around cloud in banking — any cloud
message has to look compliance-aware.

**Software engineers in Poland, Czechia and Romania.** We compete for them against product companies,
so the campaign must not make Asseco look like a legacy shop.

### The objections we know are coming

- "Asseco is a legacy dinosaur — this is old software with a new front-end."
- "Out of the box means we cannot differentiate; our bank will look like everyone else's."
- "Cloud core banking will never clear our regulator, so the subscription model is theatre."
- "Vendor lock-in — once our processes are their processes, we can never leave."
- "A Polish vendor cannot support us at the same level in Romania or Serbia."
- "We have seen the headlines about big public-sector IT projects."

The campaign is designed to survive these in public, not to avoid them.

## 5. The message

**Main message:**

> Your bank's next product does not need a two-year programme. It needs a platform that already knows
> how banking works. **Asseco BooX — your bank, out of the box.**

**Said differently for each audience:**

| Audience | Message |
|---|---|
| Executives | "Launch the product this year. Keep the core you already trust." |
| Architects | "Configuration, not forks. Documented APIs, your deployment model, your data." |
| Press and regulators | "Built in Poland, for European supervision — cloud, hybrid or on-premise." |
| Engineers | "We build the systems half of Polish banking runs on. Come build the next one." |

**Tone of voice:** confident, plain, unhyped. Asseco does not shout. We are the vendor you call when
failure is not an option. No startup vocabulary — no "disrupt", no "game-changer", no "revolution". And
no apologising for our size or our history; the scale is the proof.

## 6. Channels and what goes on them

| Channel | Budget share | What we do there |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn | 40% | Launch posts, paid targeting by job title, executives posting in their own voice |
| Trade press & analysts | 20% | Embargoed launch, Celent and Forrester briefings, one case study |
| Events | 15% | Impact'26 Poznań, Money20/20 Europe, round-tables in Warsaw, Prague, Bucharest |
| X / Twitter | 15% | Short technical threads aimed at architects, in English |
| Reddit & communities | 10% | One announced AMA with the BooX chief architect |

**LinkedIn launch post (approved):**

> Twelve months to launch a new savings product. That is the average in CEE retail banking. We think
> that number should be a lot smaller.
> Asseco BooX ships with the processes already built — onboarding, lending, deposits, cards, servicing —
> so your team configures a product instead of running a programme. Keep your core. Choose your
> deployment: cloud, hybrid, or your own data centre.
> Your bank, out of the box.

**X post (approved):**

> "Out of the box" usually means "you will be fighting it by month three".
> So we published the process library and the API docs before the sales deck.
> Asseco BooX — configure the product, keep your core, pick your deployment.
> Read the docs first, talk to us second. #corebanking #fintech

**On Reddit and developer communities, the rule is strict:** anyone from Asseco who joins a discussion
says in the comment that they work for Asseco. No agency accounts, no paid or incentivised posts, no
pretending to be a customer. We expect this to be the most hostile channel and the most useful one,
because the architect audience actually lives there.

| 2 — Launch | 1–20 Oct 2026 | BooX revealed, documentation portal goes live, press embargo lifts |

## 8. Communication policy

**The standing rules:**

1. Every public claim must be traceable to a signed document. Marketing does not invent numbers.
2. Client names appear only with that client's written approval, case by case.
3. No competitor is ever named in Asseco creative.
4. Employees taking part in public discussion disclose that they work for Asseco.
5. Anything touching regulation or compliance is cleared by Legal before publication.
6. Prospect data is handled under GDPR. No scraped contact lists.

**Answers we have pre-approved:**

- *On "you are legacy":* "def3000 is running in production in more than half of Polish banking today.
  BooX is what we built for the next product, not a rename of the last one. The architecture
  documentation is public — judge it on that."
- *On lock-in:* "The process library is configurable and the APIs are documented and public. We do not
  consider a customer retained if they stay because leaving is hard."
- *On cloud and the regulator:* "BooX runs on-premise, hybrid or in the cloud. Which one you choose is a
  conversation between you and your supervisor, and we support all three."
- *On regional support:* "Asseco is a federation of local companies. In Romania you are supported by a
  Romanian Asseco company, under one group contract."

**If the reaction turns negative:**

| Level | Situation | What we do | Who owns it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Normal questions and scepticism | Answer publicly within 4 hours, on the facts, link the docs | Social team |
| 2 | Sustained technical criticism of our claims | The architect answers in their own name within 24 hours — not in brand voice | BooX product lead |
| 3 | Accusation of misleading claims, picked up by press | Statement from Group Communication, pause paid spend on that creative | Head of Communication |
| 4 | Regulatory or client-confidentiality exposure | Full stop, Legal leads, management board informed | Management Board |

**We stop the campaign completely if:** a claim turns out to be unsupportable, a named client objects
publicly, a live BooX implementation has a publicised incident, or positive/neutral sentiment stays
below 50% for seven days in a row.

## 9. Budget

**PLN 4.8 million** across the whole window.
LinkedIn 40% · trade press and analysts 20% · events 15% · X 15% · community and content 10%.
PLN 600,000 is held back centrally and released only once the phase-3 proof material exists.

## 10. What success looks like

A chief architect at a bank that has never taken an Asseco call reads our API documentation on their
own, unprompted, and forwards it to their COO with the words *"this one is actually worth a meeting."*

Everything else in this brief exists to produce that sentence.
